battle.name: 第二次長州征討
battle.theater: 下關海峽與萩城高砂一線
battle.brief: 一八六六年朝廷再下第二次征討長州的勅旨，官軍以第一、第五師團攻入周防，關門海峽被岸砲逐退，九月十五日高砂之役更被長州奇兵隊打崩，圍困萩城到冬天，最後講和撤軍。卡面這艘一八六二年英國鐵甲艦沒有到過日本：長州要自己造它，幕府要向歐洲買它，決定勝負的其實是兵站與彈藥。

kit.name: 鐵甲艦
kit.history: 木殼外面包了鐵。裝甲第一次比砲更難對付，砲塔的設計從此繞著它轉。

countries: 第二次長州征討的交戰雙方，是一八六六年朝廷（新政府）一方的官軍與長州藩聯軍，幕府的位置最為微妙。官軍方面，孝明天皇在慶應二年下第二次征討長州的勅旨，兵部掌軍政、軍務官綜理軍備與運輸，作戰序列以第一師團與第五師團兩支為主：第五師團是由熊本藩出身的士官組成的新式部隊，擔任正面攻擊，第一師團負責海上輸送與山口以西的佈防；此外還有薩摩藩兵、各藩派來的義師與朝廷直屬的隊伍，總指揮由朝廷任命。幕府方面表面上服從朝廷的勅旨，暗地裡卻與長州合作：幕府的艦隊與砲台在關門海峽一線與長州並肩作戰，金雲坂一役亦有幕府方的人馬在長州陣內，理由很直白——幕府寧願看新政府在此役折損，也不願朝廷的權威坐大。長州一方以藩主毛利元治為名義首腦，實際作戰落到高杉晉作所率的奇兵隊與諸隊手中，防守核心是萩城與門戶洞門、下關的海岸砲台，談判由藩廳老吏與毛利家臣經手。外國各國在此役保持中立，沒有任何一國出兵或介入交火，留下的只是幕府的借款、外國商行的槍砲生意，以及各國航海日誌裡零星記載的海峽炮聲。
countriesEn: The two sides in the Second Chōshū Expedition were the imperial forces of the court, the new government, in 1866 and the army of the Chōshū domain, with the shogunate occupying the most awkward position of the three. On the government side Emperor Kōmei issued the second mandate to punish Chōshū in the second year of Keiō, the War Ministry directed the campaign and a military affairs official handled armament and transport, and the order of battle rested on two divisions: the Fifth Division, a new-style force made up of officers from Kumamoto domain, which was to make the frontal attack, and the First Division, responsible for sealift and for the line west of Yamaguchi; besides these came Satsuma troops, contingents sent by other domains and units directly under the court, with a commander appointed by the court. The shogunate on the surface obeyed the mandate but in secret cooperated with Chōshū: shogunate ships and batteries fought shoulder to shoulder with Chōshū on the Shimonoseki line, and shogunate men stood in the Chōshū line at the battle of Kin'yūmon, for a very plain reason — the shogunate would rather see the new government bleed in this campaign than see the court's authority grow. On the Chōshū side the nominal head was the domain lord Mōri Motoharu, while the actual fighting was run by Takasugi Shinsaku's Kiheitai and the other corps; the core of the defence was Hagi castle together with the coastal batteries at the mouths of the strait and at Shimonoseki, and the negotiations were handled by the senior officials of the Hagi domain office and the Mōri retainers. The foreign powers stood aside throughout: not one of them put troops into the field or intervened in the exchanges, and what they left behind was the shogunate's borrowing, the arms trade of the foreign merchants, and the occasional sound of gunfire in the strait as recorded in various captains' journals.
people: 推動這場戰爭的只有少數幾個人。朝廷一方，孝明天皇在慶應元年秋下第二次征討的勅旨，一八六七年一月三十日在征討尚未收束時病逝，朝野多把這件事與征長受挫連在一起；兵部與軍務官層面，掌軍政的是大久保利通，綜理軍備與購艦的是大村益次郎，他在京都與幕府之間往來周旋，把軍艦與槍械的管道握在手裡。前線上，第五師團是一支精銳的新式部隊，團長是熊本藩出身的少將，卻在高砂陣地前被打崩，部隊連夜退回；隨第一師團西行的年輕少佐山縣有朋，後來成了戊辰戰爭北方戰線的主帥之一。長州一方最關鍵的是高杉晉作：他以奇兵隊司令的身分在金雲坂把第五師團打散，之後又與西鄉隆盛往返京都，最終促成薩長之間的密約；藩主毛利元治在萩城內主持和議，是朝廷與幕府都不得不對話的那一端（他的父親、前藩主毛利敬親已於一八六三年去世；當年由這位退隱老藩主作主送京的五卿，正是長州藩被朝廷視為朝敵的起點）。幕府方面，德川慶喜表面服從朝廷的勅命，私下以艦隊與砲兵支援長州，關門砲台正是這段時間由幕府聘用的法國工程師韋爾尼設計興建的。
peopleEn: Only a handful of men actually drove this war. On the court side Emperor Kōmei issued the second mandate to punish Chōshū in the autumn of the first year of Keiō and died on 30 January 1867, while the campaign was still unresolved, and the court at large tied that death to the rebuff at Chōshū; in the War Ministry and the military affairs office, Ōkubo Rikō directed the war and Ōmura Masujirō handled armament and the purchase of warships, shuttling between Kyoto and the shogunate and keeping the channels for guns and ships in his own hands. On the front line the Fifth Division was an elite new-style formation under a major general from Kumamoto domain, and it was shattered before the Takasago position, the division falling back during the night; the young major Yamagata Aritomo, who marched west with the First Division, was later to become one of the commanders on the northern front of the Boshin War. The decisive figure on the Chōshū side was Takasugi Shinsaku: as commander of the Kiheitai he broke the Fifth Division at Kin'yūmon, and afterwards he travelled to and fro between Kyoto and the domain with Saigō Takamori, until the secret understanding between Satsuma and Chōshū was struck; the domain lord Mōri Motoharu conducted the peace talks inside Hagi castle and was the counterpart whom neither the court nor the shogunate could ignore (his father, the former lord Mōri Takachika, had died in 1863; it was that retired old lord who had arranged for the five court nobles to be handed over to the capital, the step that made the domain an enemy of the throne) On the shogunate side Tokugawa Yoshinobu obeyed the court's mandate in public while supporting Chōshū with ships and artillery in private, and the Shimonoseki battery was built in exactly this stretch of time to the design of the French engineer Verny, whom the shogunate had engaged.
kits: 卡面這艘一八六二年式英國鐵甲艦並沒有出現在這場戰爭裡，但它標出的正是這場戰爭的技術分水嶺。一八六六年英國海軍有裝甲主力艦無畏號（Warrior）、一八六一年下水的普林斯·康索特級與國防號（Defence），法國有葛力埃號（Gloire）與拿破崙號（Napoléon），丹麥有一八六三年的羅夫·克拉克號（Rolf Krake），同年英國還有君主號（Monarch）下水；歐洲海戰的勝負已經由木殼轉到鐵殼——一八五五年的金布倫砲台之役、一八六三年波羅的海海戰、一八六四年的第二次石勒蘇益格戰爭與一八六五年的聖地牙哥海戰都是這條線上的節點，日本卻連一艘真正的裝甲艦都沒有。長州藩的辦法是自己造：一八六五年之後在萩的高島設造船所，造出以鐵板包覆舷側與艏樓的西式蒸氣軍艦，史家多稱之為「甲鐵艦」；幕府則在同一時期向歐洲洽購鐵甲艦，並由法國工程師韋爾尼在關門海峽設計關門砲台，用的是英式後膛重砲。真正投入交火的是新政府一方的木殼蒸汽軍艦與小型帆船，面對長州岸砲與幕府砲台的交叉火網，結果是一艘運輸船中彈起火、艦隊退出海峽。陸上，長州奇兵隊用恩菲爾德式與米尼式後膛步槍，海岸砲台用重砲；官軍主力仍是火繩銃與少量仿製洋槍，口徑與射速都落在下風。運輸靠蒸汽船把人馬送上山口以西的灘頭，再以車隊沿山陰道與山陽道輸送，補給線長而脆；長州則靠海峽封鎖與內地物資維持萩城度過冬天。
kitsEn: The British ironclad of 1862 on this card never fought in this war, but it marks exactly the technological divide on which the war turned. In 1866 the Royal Navy had the armoured capital ship Warrior, the Prince Consort class and the Defence launched in 1861, France had the Gloire and the Napoléon, Denmark had the Rolf Krake of 1863, and Britain launched the Monarch in the same year; the issue in European naval battle had already shifted from wooden to iron hulls, and the landmarks on that line are the action at the Kinburn batteries in 1855, the Baltic battle of 1863, the Second Schleswig War of 1864 and the fight off Santiago de Cuba in 1865, yet Japan did not so much as possess a single true ironclad. Chōshū's answer was to build one: after 1865 a shipyard was set up at Takasago in Hagi and a Western-style steam warship with iron plating over her sides and bow was built, which historians generally call the Kōtetsu-kan; the shogunate meanwhile opened negotiations to buy ironclads in Europe and had the French engineer Verny design the Shimonoseki battery on the strait, armed with British breech-loading heavy guns. What actually went into the exchange was the government's wooden steam warships and small sailing craft, and against the crossfire of the Chōshū shore guns and the shogunate batteries a transport was hit, caught fire, and the squadron withdrew from the strait. On land the Chōshū Kiheitai carried Enfield and Minié breech-loading rifles and the shore batteries carried heavy guns, while the government's main body still carried matchlocks and a few imitations of foreign rifles, behind in both calibre and rate of fire. Transport ran by steamers landing the troops on the beaches west of Yamaguchi, and from there by cart along the San'in and San'yō roads, a supply line long and brittle; Chōshū in turn kept Hagi through the winter on what the blockade of the strait and the interior could carry.
tactics: 官軍的打法是西式操典加正面強攻，結果全撞在高地與連續火網上。第五師團沿山陰道南下，先以艦隊控制關門海峽，再由灘頭向萩城方向推進；抵達高砂一線時，第五師團以密集隊形攻擊長州在金雲坂的陣地，前鋒帶槍刺突進，後隊在後方以野戰砲支援——但密集隊形正是後膛步槍最愛的目標，長州砲台居高臨下俯瞰整個坡面，射界與射程都佔盡，攻方的火繩銃在這種距離上根本壓不住。官軍的另一支部隊在山口方向與長州的另一批砲台對射，試圖用圍攻切斷萩城的水陸補給，卻因萩前潟湖的水道太淺，軍艦根本駛不進港內，封鎖線始終合不攏。長州方的戰法是砲台拒止加奇兵隊的反擊：先把艦隊逐出海峽，再以奇兵隊的三個中隊在夜色中逼近，待官軍的射擊稍停便以密集的白刃衝鋒接上齊射，把官軍的前頭部隊與後隊切斷，然後以優勢兵力吃掉潰散之敵；幕府方投入的隊伍在同一時段從側後方加入，使官軍腹背受敵。戰後官軍轉為長期圍城，冬季的強攻與夜襲都因火藥受潮、彈藥不足與天寒而失敗，最後是靠談判收場。
tacticsEn: The government's method was Western drill plus frontal assault, and it broke against high ground and overlapping fire. The Fifth Division marched south along the San'in road, took control of the Shimonoseki Strait with the squadron first, and then pushed inland from the beaches toward Hagi; when it reached the Takasago line it attacked the Chōshū position at Kin'yūmon in close order, the leading files going forward with bayonets and the supporting guns firing from the rear, but a close-order formation is exactly what a breech-loading rifle feeds on, and the Chōshū batteries looked down the whole slope with the range and the field of fire both in their favour, while at that distance the attackers' matchlocks could not answer at all. Another government column matched batteries with batteries toward Yamaguchi and tried to cut the water and land supply of Hagi by blockade, but the channel into Hagi ran through a lagoon too shallow for warships to enter, so the cordon never closed. The Chōshū method was refusal by battery followed by a counter-stroke from the Kiheitai: first drive the squadron out of the strait, then bring the three companies of the Kiheitai forward under cover of night, and the moment the government fire slackened charge home in massed order with the volley coming on the heels of the bayonets, cutting the leading files off from the rear, and then closing on the broken units with superior numbers; a shogunate contingent joined in the same hours from the flank and rear, so that the government was taken between two sides. After the defeat the government settled down to a long siege, and the winter assaults and night attacks all failed because the powder was damp, the ammunition short and the cold bitter, and the campaign was settled by negotiation instead.
data: 可核對的數字大致如下。第一次長州征討於一八六四年十一月以講和收場，條款之一是第二次討伐延後一年執行，故第二次征討的時間表先定在慶應元年秋，其後再議改到慶應二年。真正打開的是慶應二年八月：西曆一八六六年九月五日是關門海峽的交火日，舊曆八月十七日即西曆九月十五日是金雲坂之戰，同日第五師團崩潰。兵員方面，兩支師團加上薩摩藩兵與各藩義師，總數以萬人計；第五師團本身是數千人的規模，長州方面的奇兵隊約五六百人，加上諸隊與藩兵，總數在千餘人上下，萩城守備為數百人。海峽一役，新政府一方記為一艘運輸船中彈起火沉沒或被放棄、數艘受傷，長州與幕府一方沒有失去船隻，艦隊退回外海。距離上，下關海峽到萩城海路約三十公里，豐浦到萩城沿山陰道約五十公里，萩城到高砂的金雲坂陣地約十餘公里；萩四面圍山、耕地有限，冬季圍城期間城內糧食見底，這也是和談得以迅速成交的原因。砲與槍械上，長州與幕府在關門與萩一線佈置的西洋式重砲約十數門，藩兵使用的英製恩菲爾德與米尼式後膛步槍數量在數百支以上，幕府的關門砲台採用英式後膛砲，新政府一方則靠小石川工場仿製的洋槍逐步換裝。各家日文史料對兵員與傷亡的記載差異頗大，上述數字應視為量級而非定論。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked run roughly as follows. The First Chōshū Expedition was brought to an end by a settlement in November 1864, and one of the terms of that settlement was that the second punitive expedition was to be deferred by about a year, so the timetable for the second expedition was first set for the autumn of the first year of Keiō and then moved on to the second year. What actually opened was the eighth month of the second year of Keiō: 5 September 1866 by the Gregorian calendar was the day of the engagement in the Shimonoseki Strait, and the seventeenth day of the eighth lunar month, that is 15 September, was the battle of Kin'yūmon, on which the Fifth Division collapsed. On numbers of men, the two divisions together with the Satsuma troops and the contingents of the other domains came to a force counted in thousands, on the order of ten thousand; the Fifth Division itself was a formation of some thousands; on the Chōshū side the Kiheitai numbered about five or six hundred men, and with the other corps and the domain troops the total was in the region of a thousand, with some hundreds manning Hagi castle. In the engagement in the strait the government side is credited with one transport struck, set on fire and either sunk or abandoned and several ships damaged, while neither Chōshū nor the shogunate lost a vessel, the squadron falling back to the outer sea. On distances, it is about thirty kilometres by sea from the Shimonoseki Strait to Hagi, about fifty kilometres along the San'in road from Toyoura to Hagi, and a little over ten kilometres from Hagi castle to the Kin'yūmon position at Takasago; Hagi is ringed by mountains and has little arable land, and during the winter siege the grain inside the castle ran out, which is why the talks could be concluded so quickly. On guns and small arms, the Western heavy guns posted by Chōshū and the shogunate along the Shimonoseki and Hagi lines numbered something like a dozen or more, the British Enfield and Minié breech-loading rifles held by the domain troops ran to several hundred, the shogunate's Shimonoseki battery used British breech-loading pieces, and on the government side the imitations of foreign rifles made at the Koishikawa works were put into service by degrees. The Japanese records differ considerably on strengths and casualties, and the figures above should be read as orders of magnitude rather than as settled fact.
cause: 打起來有兩層原因，第一層是字面上的約定。第一次長州征討在一八六四年以講和收場，講和的一個交換條件就是朝廷保留再次討伐長州的權利，討伐被推遲約一年，作為長州整頓內部與求得喘息時間的交換。因此第二次征討不是突發的戰爭，而是一份尚未兌現的合約；問題只在於兌現的時候，長州手裡已經多了什麼。答案是多了很多：一八六五年前後，長州藩把藩政大權交到高杉晉作與一系改革派手中，設立奇兵隊等洋式部隊，聘請外國教練，在萩與下關沿岸修築西洋式砲台，在高島興建造船所，購置西式船隻與重砲，槍械多經大坂的池田屋等商行輸入；同一時期幕府睜一眼閉一眼，關門砲台便是幕府一方出錢出技師興建的。第二層是政治：新政府成立後需要一場對外的勝利來證明自己的正統與武力，而薩摩藩的態度使這一役非打不可——薩摩的藩兵隨官軍出動，長州一旦被消滅，等於消滅了新政府自己的一支力量。朝廷內部也清楚知道這一役不好打：西鄉隆盛以薩摩代表的身份在京都往來，事先為長州爭取到延後的時間，徵討的實際命令下到一半，薩長之間的密約也已在暗中成形。
causeEn: There were two layers to the cause, the first of them literal. The First Chōshū Expedition was closed by a settlement in 1864, and one of the terms of that settlement was that the court kept the right to punish Chōshū again, with the punishing deferred by about a year in exchange for time to settle the domain's internal affairs and get its breath. The Second Chōshū Expedition was therefore not a sudden war but an agreement that had yet to be cashed in, and the only question was what Chōshū would be holding when the time came. The answer was a great deal: around 1865 the domain handed power to Takasugi Shinsaku and the reforming faction, raised Western-style units such as the Kiheitai, engaged foreign instructors, built Western batteries along the coasts of Hagi and Shimonoseki, set up a shipyard at Takasago, and bought Western steamers and heavy guns, with much of the small arms coming through houses such as Ikedaya in Osaka; over the same period the shogunate looked the other way, and the Shimonoseki battery was in fact paid for and engineered by the shogunate. The second layer was political: the new government needed a victory over some foreign enemy to make good its own legitimacy and its armed strength, and the attitude of Satsuma made the campaign impossible to avoid, for Satsuma's own troops marched with the government armies, and the destruction of Chōshū would have meant the destruction of a force the new government itself depended on. The court also understood that this war would be hard: Saigō Takamori, acting for Satsuma in Kyoto, had already bought time for Chōshū, and while the orders for the campaign were still going out the secret compact between Satsuma and Chōshū was taking shape in private.
impact: 這一役的後果，第一層在戰爭技術上。日本用這場戰爭學到的第一課是：洋式槍砲本身並不等於勝利，金雲坂一役決定勝負的是射擊紀律、居高臨下的射界與兵力的集中，而這些都要靠後勤與訓練撐住。官軍從此把野戰砲、彈藥定裝與兵站列為重點，長州也把建造艦隊列入國策，一八六六年之後日本開始出現自己的裝甲艦工程。幕府的關門砲台由法國工程師韋爾尼主持設計，成為日本近代砲台建築的樣板，後來歸入新政府的海防體系。第二層在政局，這才是關鍵。孝明天皇在第二次征討受挫、萩城未下、朝野議論紛紛之際病逝，一八六七年一月三十日的消息讓「王師不能討平朝敵」成為攻擊幕府的最好材料；同年十月德川慶喜上表奉還政權，一八六八年戊辰戰爭開打，江戶城在一月三日開城。而長州因為打了這一仗，證明自己不可輕犯，也證明自己是新政府無法繞過的力量，它在同年五月進京，薩摩與長州在倒幕的帳簿上正式結清。第三層在海軍：幕府在同一時期向歐洲洽購的鐵甲艦，隨著政權更替落到新政府手中，成為日本海軍最早的一批鐵甲艦；海峽的砲火則讓關門兩岸的砲台在往後數十年裡一直是日本海防的第一道線。
impactEn: The consequences of this campaign come in three layers, the first of them technical. The first lesson Japan drew from this war was that Western guns and rifles were not in themselves victory: what decided Kin'yūmon was shooting discipline, the field of fire from the high ground and the concentration of strength, and all of those had to be carried by logistics and training. The government thereafter made field artillery, fixed ammunition and lines of supply its priorities, and Chōshū entered warship building as a matter of state policy, so that from 1866 onward Japan began to have ironclad projects of its own. The Shimonoseki battery, designed under the French engineer Verny, became the model of modern Japanese battery construction and later passed into the new government's coastal defence system. The second layer is political, and it is the layer that mattered. Emperor Kōmei died while the second expedition was still unresolved, with Hagi untaken and the capital full of talk, and the news of his death on 30 January 1867 supplied the best possible material for the attack on the shogunate; in the following October Tokugawa Yoshinobu tendered the transfer of authority, the Boshin War opened in 1868, and Edo castle was opened on the third of January. Chōshū, having fought this war, had shown both that it could not be treated lightly and that the new government could not go around it, and it entered the capital in May of that same year, with Satsuma and Chōshū square accounts in the ledger of the overthrow. The third layer is naval: the ironclads the shogunate was negotiating for in Europe passed with the change of government into the hands of the new administration and became among the first ironclads of the Japanese navy, while the gunfire in the strait left the batteries on both shores of the Shimonoseki as the first line of Japanese coastal defence for decades afterwards.
result: 結果是官軍沒有攻下萩城，長州也沒有被消滅，戰事以一八六六年的失敗和講和收場。海峽一役之後，官軍的攻勢在金雲坂停住，此後整整一個冬天都圍著萩城打，打不進城也撤不出來，最後靠談判解決：一八六七年朝廷與長州之間達成講和，核心是藩主毛利元治暫不上京、萩城的處置延後，朝廷自長州境內撤出駐軍，戰爭以撤軍收尾。雙方都沒有得到想要的東西：朝廷沒有雪恥，新政府的正統反而受損，於是把力量轉向江戶，同年十月德川慶喜奉還政權，一八六八年正月江戶城開城，戊辰戰爭把幕府連根拔起；長州則從「朝敵」變成新政府的柱石，一八六八年五月以薩長聯軍的身份入京。一八六六年九月那幾天在海峽與高砂分出的勝負，最後是在次年江戶城開城的那一天才真正結清。卡面這艘一八六二年式英國鐵甲艦最終沒有到過日本，卻是這一役的隱形主角：長州要自己造它，幕府要向歐洲買它，新政府連一艘能擋住它的船都沒有，而最後決定這場征討的不是裝甲，是兵站、彈藥與政治現實。
resultEn: The result was that the government did not take Hagi and Chōshū was not destroyed; the war ended in a defeat for the government in 1866 and a negotiated peace. After the engagement in the strait the government offensive stopped dead at Kin'yūmon, and for the whole of the following winter it sat before Hagi, unable to force the castle and unable to get away, and the matter was settled by negotiation: in 1867 the court and Chōshū reached an understanding whose substance was that the domain lord Mōri Motoharu would not yet go up to the capital and that the disposal of Hagi was put off, the government withdrawing its troops from Chōshū territory, and the war was closed by that withdrawal. Neither side got what it wanted. The court was not avenged, the legitimacy of the new government was damaged instead, and it turned its strength towards Edo, where in the same October Tokugawa Yoshinobu restored the authority to the throne and in January 1868 Edo castle was opened and the Boshin War pulled the shogunate up by the roots. Chōshū turned from the empire's enemy into a pillar of the new government and entered the capital in May 1868 with the Satsuma-Chōshū forces. The result of those few days in September 1866 in the strait and at Takasago was finally settled on the day in the following year when Edo castle was opened. The British ironclad of 1862 on this card never reached Japan, and yet it is the hidden protagonist of this campaign: Chōshū meant to build one, the shogunate meant to buy one from Europe, the new government could not muster a single ship that would stand against such a thing, and what settled the expedition in the end was not armour but supply, ammunition and political reality.
